Fluency and Coherence
Grammatical Range and Accuracy
Lexical Resource
Pronunciation

pro_course_detail.title: OPEN  CONVERSATION (SPEAKING & FLUENCY PRACTICE)
pro_course_detail.description:
My class sessions mainly start with open conversations that allow me to learn about my student and also make an assessment of how best can help them make improvements. I like to ask the student what goals or targets they may have.
The lesson plan carters for General English depending on the preference of the student.
In this lesson, students learn and practice vocabulary to talk about a city break. Exercises cover places to go, what to pack and how to get around a city. There is also a grammar activity on there was/there were, in which students complete.
In the lesson package, students learn the structure like, don't like, hate, love + -ing. Students listen to a short conversation about likes and dislikes. There is also an online video-aided exercise in which students watch a series of video clips and make sentences using the target language.

The third lesson introduces elementary students to the present continuous. The target language is presented in a dialogue and there are several activities in which students practice the new structure. The worksheet also presents expressions for describing typical holiday/vacation activities and revises language from previous lessons.

In the next lesson, Students define free-time activities and listen to a conversation between two people with different lifestyles. They learn how to ask present simple questions about habits and routines and how to use adverbs of frequency in their answers. Students interview their partners about exercise and food habits. There is also a short optional extension activity related to sports collocations with the verbs go, play, and do.
By the 5th lesson, Students revise and extend phrases to describe leisure activities and listen to two short interviews about how people spend their free time. The language point is (really) + like/love/hate/prefer + verb with -ing. Students practice the target language in a speaking activity and there is a short optional extension activity

pro_course_detail.title: TEST  PREPARATION ( IELTS)  & INTERVIEW PREPARATION
pro_course_detail.description:
This lesson caters to students who are either preparing for their examinations such as the IELTS and the Cambridge B2 First exam or those who are preparing to attend a job interview as well as students who need to interview candidates in English.
A level placement test has been designed to be used for determining a student's level according to his/her speaking ability and categorized into one of the following: Elementary, Pre-intermediate, Intermediate, Upper intermediate-advance.
This lesson plan is designed to prepare IELTS candidates to talk about different topics in Parts 1, 2, and 3 of the IELTS Speaking test.

The lesson includes a topic on Expressing Opinions. In the IELTS speaking test, the examiner will ask for the candidate's opinions on different topics. This lesson plan gives students practice in expressing their opinions using a variety of structures
In the IELTS speaking test, the examiner might ask difficult questions and the candidate may need some time to think about how to respond. This lesson plan gives students practice in using 'time fillers' -- words and structures that allow them to buy time to think without affecting their fluency score.
For the students who will be preparing for a Job interview, the class will take the following approach:
The worksheet presents key adjectives for describing personal characteristics as well as common words and expressions used for writing a CV. Students look at a variety of typical questions that can be asked during a job interview and then listen to a dialogue between an interviewer and a candidate. The language used in the dialogue is studied and practiced through role play. 

In this dialogue-based lesson plan, students learn useful vocabulary for attending a job interview in English. The worksheet includes an article about things candidates shouldn't say during an interview.
Students identify and compare some jobs and then listen to/read a text about a typical day in the life of the workers.
